findings.F1: The book sizes against its own effect: the vol-target sizing holds a mean position of 0.56 on Mondays in the lowest pooled tercile of 30-day hourly volatility, where the reversal is nil (-0.004 %, t -0.03, n 604; position-weighted -0.17 %), but only 0.21 on the highest tercile, where the reversal is +0.98 % per case (t 3.27, n 604); the middle tercile gives +0.56 % (t 3.06) at a position of 0.36.
findings.F2: Fees take all of what the book captures: its 3746 trades gain +0.098 % on average before fees and -0.003 % after; one trade costs 0.19 %, more than the whole low-volatility Monday move (≈0 %) but a fifth of the high-volatility one (0.98 %). That is why the mean daily return on days in a position is 0.0099 % against the 0.05 % required.
findings.F3: Its losses sit in the low-volatility years: the book lost in 2023 (-6.8 % summed daily returns), 2024 (-4.1 %) and 2025 (-5.6 %). In 2023, 166 of 224 Mondays fell in the lowest volatility tercile, and only 10 in the highest. The deepest fall (-16.8 %, 310 days) sits in those stretches, so a 0.7 % yearly return gives a Calmar of 0.04.
findings.F4: High volatility is not an effect of its own. On other days of the week, a day's 24-hour move is reversed over the next 24 hours by only +0.12 % (t 1.75, n 7281) in the highest volatility tercile, against +0.98 % after a Sunday at the same volatility. Monday's reversal at high volatility is not a general drift either: Monday's unsigned excess move is -0.23 % (t -0.77). The volatility grading is the idea's own stated condition.
findings.F5: It is the level of hourly volatility that grades the reversal, not volatility relative to the coin's own past six months: across terciles of that ratio the reversal is -0.35 %, +0.14 % and +0.01 % (all |t| < 1.1, n ≈ 200 each).
findings.F6: The reversal keeps going into Tuesday. Over 48 hours it is +0.58 % per case (t 3.82, n 2404) against +0.39 % over 24 hours (t 3.61), with hours 24–48 alone adding +0.21 % (t 2.19). In the highest volatility tercile it grows from +0.98 % to +1.37 % (t 3.49), and in the middle one from +0.56 % to +0.99 % (t 4.09).
findings.F7: The down-Sunday side carries most of it: after a falling Sunday the coin rises +0.55 % over Monday (t 3.73, n 1247), while after a rising Sunday it falls +0.22 % (t 1.40, n 1178).
findings.F8: Sunday's largest moves are not reversed more. The top fifth by size of Sunday's move in usual moves (mean 2.2) reverses +0.22 % (t 0.70), against +0.55 % to +0.67 % in the other four fifths, yet the book gives that fifth its largest position (0.83).

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Sunday, measured against the coin's usual 30-day move, is followed over Monday and Tuesday (the next 48 hours) by a move in the opposite direction whose size as a share of price grows with the coin's 30-day hourly volatility, so the reversal is largest in the coin's most volatile months and near nothing in its calmest.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean against Sunday's move with a stake that rises with the coin's hourly volatility, not falls with it, hold it through Tuesday, and refuse it when the coin is calm and the move cannot cover the fee.
ideas.name: Volatile Sunday reversal over two days

ideas.idea: A coin's fall over Sunday's 24 hours, measured against its usual 30-day move, is followed over the next 48 hours (Monday and Tuesday) by a rise, the larger the higher the coin's 30-day hourly volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy after a falling Sunday in a volatile coin and hold through Tuesday, leaving out the weaker short after a rising Sunday.
ideas.name: Sunday falls rebound early week

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return over Sunday, measured against its usual 30-day move, is followed over the next 48 hours by an opposite move that grows with the product of that scaled Sunday move, up to about two usual moves, and the coin's 30-day hourly volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size the lean against Sunday's move by its size times the coin's hourly volatility, and not let the most extreme Sundays take the largest stake.
ideas.name: Moderate Sunday moves reverse most
